content: 1. Follow the manufacturer's color-coding to differentiate between active and inert tablets. Begin the regimen on the first day of the menstrual cycle or the Sunday following the start of the cycle. Take one hormonally active tablet orally for 21 consecutive days, followed by 7 days without tablets or with inert tablets, as provided. Repeat the cycle. 2. The risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases after delivery when using combined hormonal contraceptives. This risk decreases rapidly after 21 days postpartum but does not return to baseline until 42 days postpartum. According to CDC guidelines, postpartum women without additional VTE risk factors should wait 3–6 weeks before initiating combined hormonal contraceptives. Specifically: After vaginal delivery: Wait at least 3 weeks. After cesarean section: Wait at least 6 weeks. Women with additional VTE risk factors postpartum should not use combined hormonal contraceptives. 3. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with CYP1A2 inhibitors (weak, moderate, or strong) increases fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration. 4. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, with some cases >20x ULN). Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before starting this hepatitis C combination therapy. Restart ethinyl estradiol-containing medications approximately 2 weeks after completing the hepatitis C regimen. 5. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Amobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 7. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 8. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A4 substrates may result in reduced therapeutic effects. Monitor for loss of efficacy and adjust doses as needed. 9. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 11. Belzutifan reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding may occur. Advise women of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 12. Bosentan reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Brigatinib reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and brigatinib may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 14. Butabarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Calaspargase pegol may interact indirectly with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Avoid concomitant use. Use non-oral contraceptive methods for females of childbearing potential. 16. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during and for 1 week after elagolix treatment. 21. Elvitegravir reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 22. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, adjust substrate dosages as per prescribing information. 23. Encorafenib reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and encorafenib may cause fetal harm. Use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose. 24. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 25.
